small_guidance:
- Add autotune configs that tile the OH*OW spatial axis more aggressively with smaller BLOCK_OC (e.g. BLOCK_N=64/BLOCK_OC=64 num_warps=4, BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_OC=32 num_warps=4) — at OC=64 a BLOCK_OC of 64 means many configs only span 1 OC tile and waste OC parallelism; smaller OC tiles with more programs may saturate SMs better.
- Hoist the `oh*IW+ow` computation and reuse it; also try swapping pid order (pid_b on axis 0, pid_n on axis 2) to improve L2 reuse of the weight tile across batches via persistent OC programs.
- Try loading the weight tile once per (kh,kw,ic) into registers across multiple batches by adding a BLOCK_B loop (fuse batch into the program), reducing redundant weight loads.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an im2col-style GEMM with a K-loop over IC*KH*KW (=72) as the inner reduction and a real `tl.dot` on BLOCK_M×BLOCK_K × BLOCK_K×BLOCK_N tiles. The current kernel does scalar FMAs (`x[:,None]*w[None,:]`) instead of using tensor cores — this is the main reason it stays at fast_p≈0.88. With M=OH*OW (64516), N=OC (64), K=72, a tile like BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=32 on tensor cores should be much faster.
- Switch the input layout to NHWC (channels-last) so the K dimension (IC inside the (kh,kw,ic) gather) is contiguous and `tl.load` of the K-tile coalesces; do a one-time permute of x and reshape weights to (OC, KH*KW*IC) accordingly. Keep bias-sub-Mish fused in the epilogue exactly as now.
- Consider a split-K or persistent-CTA design only after the dot-based version lands; with K=72 a single-pass GEMM with the inner reduction fully unrolled (KH*KW static, IC loop) is likely sufficient.
